title: Central clearing and the pricing of specialness in repo markets
summary: ECB Working Paper No 3214 examines how the structure of euro area interbank repo market clearing—bilateral OTC versus central counterparty (CCP)—affects the pricing of specialness in repo transactions. The paper develops a theoretical model showing repo rates are non-linear in borrower default risk, generating a systematic CCP-OTC differential. Empirical analysis using euro-area MMSR transaction-level data around the COVID-19 shock finds the CCP-OTC differential compressed by roughly 6 basis points, with compression stronger for high-quality collateral and weaker for riskier borrowers.
key_points: In OTC markets, repo rates reflect borrower-specific risk; in CCP markets, rates reflect the average risk of the participant pool, causing systematic CCP-OTC pricing wedge
Repo rates are a non-linear function of borrower default risk; averaging borrower-specific OTC prices yields more negative rates than pricing the pooled borrower in CCP markets
During COVID-19 uncertainty shock, CCP-OTC differential compressed sharply as lenders became more concerned about distribution of borrower types, raising CCP rates toward OTC levels
Borrowing costs in CCP markets increased relative to OTC markets by approximately 6 basis points following the COVID-19 shock
Compression was weaker for riskier borrowers (measured by NPL ratios and CDS spreads) and stronger for high-quality collateral (core euro-area government bonds)
Central clearing dampens specialness in normal times but stabilizes repo pricing during stress by reducing dispersion in borrower-specific rates
why_it_matters: This research illuminates a fundamental trade-off in market structure design for repo clearing. Identity-based bilateral OTC markets allow granular, risk-sensitive pricing but may be fragile during stress when counterparty relationships deteriorate. CCPs pool risk and provide anonymity, reducing price dispersion and acting as shock absorbers, but also redistribute risk and alter collateral pricing. For central banks relying on repo markets for monetary policy transmission, understanding these mechanisms is crucial for assessing central clearing policies and collateral framework design.
market_structure_context: The paper directly addresses repo market plumbing—specifically how clearing venue choice (OTC vs CCP) affects equilibrium pricing of collateral. CCPs introduce anonymity and counterparty pooling that systematically compress specialness in normal times but provide stability during stress. The research uses transaction-level MMSR data to empirically test theoretical predictions about the CCP-OTC differential across market conditions.
important_numbers: 6 basis points (CCP-OTC differential compression during COVID-19 shock)
notes: Source is an ECB Working Paper Series publication (No 3214) by Danisewicz, Dieler, Mancini, Mazzari, and Metzler. Disclaimer notes views are those of authors and not the ECB. Publication year estimated as 2024 based on paper number sequencing. Source is highly relevant to market structure focus as it examines clearing infrastructure and its effects on repo market pricing dynamics. The paper provides empirical evidence from the March 2020 COVID-19 shock to validate theoretical predictions about CCP-OTC pricing differentials.
